subject: P4 Science
source: El-Moasser Science Fourth Primary First Term 2027
sourceNote: Rebuilt lesson-by-lesson from the uploaded book contents and curriculum objectives.

modules.title: Let's Find Living Organisms
modules.summary: Living organisms can be distinguished from non-living things by life characteristics such as feeding, growth and breathing.
focus: Recognize feeding, growth and breathing as life characteristics
terms: A living thing such as a human, animal or plant
The place where a living organism lives

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Let's Find Living Organisms"?
questions.answer: Plants are living organisms because they grow and need resources.
choices: Plants are living organisms because they grow and need resources.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Rocks and water are non-living things.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A living thing such as a human, animal or plant = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Let's Find Living Organisms".
questions.answer: Plants are living organisms because they grow and need resources. Rocks and water are non-living things.

modules.title: How to Observe
modules.summary: Scientists use senses and simple tools to observe living things carefully and describe visible features.
focus: Choose safe tools for observing small details
terms: To look carefully and collect information
A tool that makes small details look larger

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "How to Observe"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: A magnifying glass helps us see small features.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: To look carefully and collect information = ______.
Explain one important idea from "How to Observe".
questions.answer: Observation means collecting details carefully. A magnifying glass helps us see small features.

modules.title: Colors and Shapes of Living Organisms
modules.summary: Living organisms differ in color, shape and external features. These differences help us describe and compare them.
focus: Compare organisms by color and shape
Use visible properties to classify observations
terms: The form or outline of an object

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Colors and Shapes of Living Organisms"?
questions.answer: Color and shape are observable properties.
choices: Color and shape are observable properties.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Different organisms may have different external features.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A visible or measurable characteristic = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Colors and Shapes of Living Organisms".
questions.answer: Color and shape are observable properties. Different organisms may have different external features.

modules.title: Different Places, Different Living Organisms
modules.summary: Habitats provide living organisms with needs such as water, food and shelter; different habitats support different organisms.
terms: A place that provides an organism's needs
A protected place for an organism

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Different Places, Different Living Organisms"?
questions.answer: Living organisms live where their needs can be met.
choices: Living organisms live where their needs can be met.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Different habitats have different conditions.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A place that provides an organism's needs = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Different Places, Different Living Organisms".
questions.answer: Living organisms live where their needs can be met. Different habitats have different conditions.

modules.title: Desert Living Organisms
modules.summary: Desert organisms have features and behaviors that help them survive heat and limited water.
focus: Relate body features and behavior to survival
terms: A feature or behavior that helps survival

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Desert Living Organisms"?
questions.answer: Desert organisms must cope with little water.
choices: Desert organisms must cope with little water.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Some desert animals avoid the hottest times of day.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A very dry habitat = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Desert Living Organisms".
questions.answer: Desert organisms must cope with little water. Some desert animals avoid the hottest times of day.

modules.title: Eggs and Larvae
modules.summary: Many insects begin life as eggs and hatch into larvae that feed and grow.
focus: Describe the beginning of an insect life cycle
terms: The first stage in many insect life cycles
A young stage that feeds and grows

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Eggs and Larvae"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Larvae usually feed and grow rapidly.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: The first stage in many insect life cycles = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Eggs and Larvae".
questions.answer: Eggs hatch into larvae. Larvae usually feed and grow rapidly.

modules.title: Pupae and Adults
modules.summary: In complete metamorphosis, the larva changes into a pupa and later becomes an adult insect.
terms: A stage in which major body change occurs
The mature stage of an insect

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Pupae and Adults"?
questions.answer: The pupa comes after the larva.
choices: The pupa comes after the larva.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: An adult emerges after the pupal stage.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A stage in which major body change occurs = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Pupae and Adults".
questions.answer: The pupa comes after the larva. An adult emerges after the pupal stage.

modules.title: Body Structure of Adults
modules.summary: Adult insects have a body divided into three main regions and have six legs.
focus: Identify the main insect body regions
terms: Front body region of an insect
Middle body region where legs attach

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Body Structure of Adults"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: The insect body has head, thorax and abdomen.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Front body region of an insect = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Body Structure of Adults".
questions.answer: Adult insects have six legs. The insect body has head, thorax and abdomen.

modules.title: Sowing Seeds
modules.summary: Seeds need suitable conditions such as water, air and an appropriate temperature to begin germination.
focus: Describe what happens when a seed starts to grow
terms: A plant structure that can grow into a new plant
The start of growth from a seed

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Sowing Seeds"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: A seed begins to grow under suitable conditions.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A plant structure that can grow into a new plant = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Sowing Seeds".
questions.answer: Water is needed for germination. A seed begins to grow under suitable conditions.

modules.title: After Sprouting
modules.summary: After germination, roots and shoots develop and the young plant begins to make its own food as leaves grow.
terms: Plant part that absorbs water and anchors the plant
Young stem and leaves growing upward

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "After Sprouting"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Shoots grow upward toward light.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Plant part that absorbs water and anchors the plant = ______.
Explain one important idea from "After Sprouting".
questions.answer: Roots grow into the soil. Shoots grow upward toward light.

modules.title: Flowers and Fruits
modules.summary: Flowers are involved in plant reproduction; after successful reproduction, fruits can form and contain seeds.
focus: Relate flowers to fruits and seeds
Sequence flower, fruit and seed development
terms: Structure that develops and often contains seeds

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Flowers and Fruits"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Many fruits contain seeds.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Plant reproductive structure = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Flowers and Fruits".
questions.answer: Fruits can develop from flowers. Many fruits contain seeds.

modules.title: The Plant Body
modules.summary: A plant has organs such as roots, stems, leaves and flowers, each with an important function.
focus: Match each organ to its function
terms: Supports the plant and transports materials
Main organ for making food using light

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "The Plant Body"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Leaves use light to help make food.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Supports the plant and transports materials = ______.
Explain one important idea from "The Plant Body".
questions.answer: Roots absorb water from soil. Leaves use light to help make food.

modules.title: How Sunlight Travels
modules.summary: Light travels in straight lines from a source until it meets matter.
terms: A representation of the path of light

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "How Sunlight Travels"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: The Sun is a natural light source.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A representation of the path of light = ______.
Explain one important idea from "How Sunlight Travels".
questions.answer: Light travels in straight lines. The Sun is a natural light source.

modules.title: Gathering Light
modules.summary: Reflective and curved surfaces can redirect or gather light, changing where light is concentrated.
terms: Bouncing of light from a surface
A smooth surface that reflects light well

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Gathering Light"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Changing a surface can change the direction of reflected light.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Bouncing of light from a surface = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Gathering Light".
questions.answer: Mirrors reflect light. Changing a surface can change the direction of reflected light.

modules.title: Shadows and the Sun (1)
modules.summary: A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light. Shadow direction depends on the position of the light source.
focus: Relate shadow direction to light direction
terms: A dark area formed where light is blocked
Not allowing light to pass through

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Shadows and the Sun (1)"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: A shadow appears on the side away from the light source.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A dark area formed where light is blocked = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Shadows and the Sun (1)".
questions.answer: Opaque objects can form shadows. A shadow appears on the side away from the light source.

modules.title: Shadows and the Sun (2)
modules.summary: The Sun's apparent position changes during the day, so the length and direction of shadows also change.
focus: Compare morning, noon and afternoon shadows
Use shadow change as evidence of Sun position
terms: The measured size of a shadow
The Sun's apparent location in the sky

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Shadows and the Sun (2)"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: A higher Sun generally produces a shorter shadow.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: The measured size of a shadow = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Shadows and the Sun (2)".
questions.answer: Shadows change during the day. A higher Sun generally produces a shorter shadow.

modules.title: Sun and Shade
modules.summary: Shade reduces direct sunlight and can affect ground temperature and moisture.
terms: An area protected from direct sunlight
A measure of how hot or cold something is

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Sun and Shade"?
questions.answer: Direct sunlight can warm the ground.
choices: Direct sunlight can warm the ground.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Shade reduces direct sunlight.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: An area protected from direct sunlight = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Sun and Shade".
questions.answer: Direct sunlight can warm the ground. Shade reduces direct sunlight.

modules.title: How Sound Is Produced
modules.summary: Sound is produced when objects vibrate.
terms: An object that vibrates to produce sound

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "How Sound Is Produced"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Stopping a vibration can stop the sound.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A rapid back-and-forth movement = ______.
Explain one important idea from "How Sound Is Produced".
questions.answer: Vibrating objects can produce sound. Stopping a vibration can stop the sound.

modules.title: Volume of Sound and Vibration
modules.summary: Stronger vibrations usually produce louder sounds; weaker vibrations produce softer sounds.
terms: How loud or soft a sound is

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Volume of Sound and Vibration"?
questions.answer: Stronger vibrations can make louder sounds.
choices: Stronger vibrations can make louder sounds.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Volume describes loudness.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: How loud or soft a sound is = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Volume of Sound and Vibration".
questions.answer: Stronger vibrations can make louder sounds. Volume describes loudness.

modules.title: How Sound Travels
modules.summary: Sound needs a material medium and can travel through solids, liquids and gases.
focus: Explain why sound does not travel through empty space
terms: A disturbance that transfers sound energy

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "How Sound Travels"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Sound can also travel through solids and liquids.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Matter through which sound travels = ______.
Explain one important idea from "How Sound Travels".
questions.answer: Sound can travel through air. Sound can also travel through solids and liquids.

modules.title: Wind-Powered Cars
modules.summary: Moving air can exert a force and cause objects such as model cars to move.
terms: A push or pull that can change motion

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Wind-Powered Cars"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Greater wind force can change motion more.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Moving air = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Wind-Powered Cars".
questions.answer: Wind can push an object. Greater wind force can change motion more.

modules.title: Sail Size
modules.summary: The area of a sail affects how much wind force can act on it and therefore can affect motion.
focus: Relate surface area to wind effect
terms: A surface that catches moving air

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Sail Size"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Changing sail size can change the effect of wind.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A surface that catches moving air = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Sail Size".
questions.answer: A sail catches moving air. Changing sail size can change the effect of wind.

modules.title: Rubber Band-Powered Cars
modules.summary: A stretched rubber band stores energy and can exert a force that moves a model car when released.
focus: Explain how stretched rubber can cause motion
Identify stored energy in stretched rubber
terms: An elastic material that can be stretched
Able to return toward original shape after stretching

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Rubber Band-Powered Cars"?
questions.answer: Stretching a rubber band stores energy.
choices: Stretching a rubber band stores energy.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Releasing it can produce motion.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: An elastic material that can be stretched = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Rubber Band-Powered Cars".
questions.answer: Stretching a rubber band stores energy. Releasing it can produce motion.

modules.title: Power of Rubber Bands
modules.summary: The amount a rubber band is stretched and its characteristics affect the motion it can produce.
terms: Increase in length due to pulling
A change in position over time

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Power of Rubber Bands"?
questions.answer: More stretch can change the force produced.
choices: More stretch can change the force produced.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Rubber band properties affect motion.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Increase in length due to pulling = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Power of Rubber Bands".
questions.answer: More stretch can change the force produced. Rubber band properties affect motion.

modules.unit: Chapter 8: Soil, Water, and Life in Egypt
modules.title: The Relationship Between the Ground and Water
modules.summary: Water moves through and is stored differently in soils depending on particle size and spaces between particles.
focus: Compare water movement in different soils
Relate soil particle size to water behavior
terms: Mixture of mineral particles and organic matter

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "The Relationship Between the Ground and Water"?
questions.answer: Water can move through spaces in soil.
choices: Water can move through spaces in soil.
It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Different soils allow water to move at different rates.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: Mixture of mineral particles and organic matter = ______.
Explain one important idea from "The Relationship Between the Ground and Water".
questions.answer: Water can move through spaces in soil. Different soils allow water to move at different rates.

modules.unit: Chapter 8: Soil, Water, and Life in Egypt
modules.title: Transporting Giant Stone Statues
modules.summary: Ancient Egyptians could use knowledge of soil, water, friction and force to help move very heavy objects.
focus: Connect science ideas to ancient engineering
Explain how changing ground conditions can affect movement
terms: A force that resists motion between surfaces
Moving an object from one place to another

questions.text: Which statement is correct about "Transporting Giant Stone Statues"?
choices: It belongs to a different science topic.
It has no relation to living things or physical forces.

questions.text: Changing the ground surface can affect how easily a heavy object moves.
Complete using a key term from this lesson: A force that resists motion between surfaces = ______.
Explain one important idea from "Transporting Giant Stone Statues".
questions.answer: Friction resists motion. Changing the ground surface can affect how easily a heavy object moves.
